## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Venasākhajātaka* (Ja 353) is a story included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The narrative opens with the verse line "‘Though thou art now’" [SuttaCentral]. According to its framing narrative, the Buddha related the discourse while residing in the Bhesakaḷā grove near Suṁsumāragiri (Mount Crocodile) in the territory of the Bhaggas, with reference to the young prince Bodhi [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text in four languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

In terms of textual parallels, SuttaCentral records a passage-level parallel to the *Cūḷanandiyajātaka* (Ja 222) and notes that the work is mentioned in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi*) [SuttaCentral].
